title: Cisco Secure Endpoint Quarantine Failures
exclusions: Only covers files the connector detected. Threats the connector did not detect, or processes already running from memory, are not reported as quarantine failures.
evidence: Saved alert results per host with the file path and hash, plus the ticket showing the host was isolated or the file removed by hand.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Pick a Quarantine Failure from the Secure Endpoint console Events page in the last 30 days and run the search over the same window. It returns a row for that host with `failures` at 1 or more and the same file path. If the console shows none, the search should also return nothing for that window.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Download EICAR to the same host without holding it open. The connector quarantines it (event 553648143); the search counts it in `quarantined` but returns no row, because `failures` is 0.

dataSources: `index=secure_endpoint sourcetype=cisco:se` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Secure Endpoint input, which polls `GET /v1/events`. This search uses event types 2164260880 (Quarantine Failure) and 553648143 (Threat Quarantined). Each event carries `event_type`, `event_type_id`, `detection`, `severity`, `connector_guid`, `group_guids{}`, `computer.hostname`, `computer.user`, `computer.external_ip`, `computer.links.trajectory`, and for file events `file.file_name`, `file.file_path`, `file.disposition`, and `file.identity.sha256`.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Secure Endpoint input.
spl:
index=secure_endpoint sourcetype="cisco:se" event_type_id IN (2164260880, 553648143)
| eval host_name='computer.hostname', user='computer.user', sha256='file.identity.sha256', file_name='file.file_name', file_path='file.file_path', trajectory='computer.links.trajectory'
| eval outcome=if(event_type_id=2164260880, "failed", "quarantined")
| stats count(eval(outcome="failed")) as failures count(eval(outcome="quarantined")) as quarantined values(detection) as detections values(file_name) as files values(file_path) as paths values(sha256) as sha256 latest(trajectory) as trajectory by host_name connector_guid
| where failures > 0
| sort - failures
description: Finds hosts where the Secure Endpoint connector detected a threat but could not quarantine it (event type 2164260880), and shows next to it how many quarantines did succeed on the same host. Each row lists the detections, file paths, hashes, and the trajectory link.
value: A quarantine failure means the malicious file is still on the machine and may still be running. These hosts need a human straight away, usually to isolate the host and remove the file manually. Seeing successful quarantines on the same host shows whether the connector works at all there.
implementation: Collect Secure Endpoint events with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) input into `index=secure_endpoint`. Schedule every 5 minutes over the last 10 minutes and page the SOC on every row.
visualization: Alert table: host_name, failures, quarantined, detections, files, paths, sha256, trajectory. Supporting panel: quarantine failures per day over 30 days (column chart).

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide
Cisco Secure Endpoint API v1: Events
Cisco Secure Endpoint API v1: Event Types

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Files in use or on read-only media** — the connector cannot quarantine a file locked by another process or stored on a read-only share or optical disk. The threat is still real; the fix is manual.

2. **Network paths** — detections on mapped drives may fail to quarantine because the connector cannot write to the share. Clean the file on the file server.

**Suppression:** none; every failure needs follow-up. Throttle per host and hash for 1 hour.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• A Secure Endpoint API credential: in the Secure Endpoint console under Administration > API Credentials, create a read-only credential and record the client ID and API key, plus the API host for your region (for example `api.amp.cisco.com` for North America, `api.eu.amp.cisco.com` for Europe).
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API host.
• An index for Secure Endpoint data (this page uses `index=secure_endpoint`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC and endpoint teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Secure Endpoint card, and create an input with the API host, client ID, and API key. Set the index to `secure_endpoint`. The modular input polls `GET /v1/events` with a default interval of 300 seconds and writes `sourcetype=cisco:se`.
• Select the event types the input should collect. Collecting all types is simplest; if you limit them, include the event type IDs this search uses.
• In a distributed deployment run the input on one node only; the guide notes that the computers, compromises, and top-malware endpoints can produce duplicates otherwise.
• Check the events this search needs: run `index=secure_endpoint sourcetype=cisco:se event_type_id IN (2164260880, 553648143) | stats count by event_type_id` over 30 days.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=secure_endpoint sourcetype="cisco:se" event_type_id IN (2164260880, 553648143)
| eval host_name='computer.hostname', user='computer.user', sha256='file.identity.sha256', file_name='file.file_name', file_path='file.file_path', trajectory='computer.links.trajectory'
| eval outcome=if(event_type_id=2164260880, "failed", "quarantined")
| stats count(eval(outcome="failed")) as failures count(eval(outcome="quarantined")) as quarantined values(detection) as detections values(file_name) as files values(file_path) as paths values(sha256) as sha256 latest(trajectory) as trajectory by host_name connector_guid
| where failures > 0
| sort - failures
```

Understanding this SPL
• 2164260880 is Quarantine Failure and 553648143 is Threat Quarantined; reading both shows whether failure is the norm on a host.
• `count(eval(...))` counts each outcome separately in one `stats`.
• `where failures > 0` keeps only hosts with at least one failure; the quarantined count is context, not a trigger.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Endpoint console Events page filtered to Quarantine Failure for the same time range: every failure there should appear here.
• Open the `trajectory` link and confirm the file is still present on the host.
• Run `index=secure_endpoint sourcetype=cisco:se | timechart span=1h count by event_type` over 7 days; flat zero for all types for more than two intervals means the input stopped, not that the estate is clean.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 5 minutes over the last 10 minutes and page the SOC.
• Response: isolate the host from the Secure Endpoint console, remove the file manually, then run a full scan.
• Review monthly which paths fail most often; repeated failures on one share point to a connector exclusion or permissions problem to fix.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No cisco:se events and HTTP 401 in the input log: wrong client ID or API key, or the API host is for a different region from the organisation.
• Events arrive but `event_type_id` is missing: the events were indexed before JSON extraction applied; check `| fieldsummary` on one hour of data.
• Duplicate events with the same `id`: the input runs on more than one node, or the legacy AMP for Endpoints input (Splunkbase 3686) is still enabled. Keep one collector.
grandmaExplanation: When the antivirus finds something bad but cannot lock it away, the bad file is still on the computer. We raise the alarm for every one of those.
